config.theme: School PTA budget meeting for next year
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: School PTA budget meeting for next year

personas.name: Denise
personas.goals: Get a budget everyone can live with before the vote
personas.hidden_agenda: Exhausted; wants someone else to chair next year

personas.name: Carl
personas.hidden_agenda: Feels accused every time someone asks about money

personas.name: Yolanda
personas.hidden_agenda: Her own classroom grant was denied last year

personas.name: Brett
personas.role: Parent, new to the PTA, outspoken
personas.hidden_agenda: Suspects the PTA is hoarding money

pack.title: PTA budget meeting - next school year

agenda.title: Last year's actuals
agenda.goal: Agree what came in and what went out last year

agenda.title: Fundraising plan
agenda.goal: Pick next year's fundraisers and realistic targets

agenda.title: Approval and next steps
agenda.goal: Agree how the budget gets voted on

facts.statement: Field trip bus cost = $650 per bus

beats.summary: Actuals; Brett inflates the revenue and suspects a hoard
What to keep; Denise misstates the fun run and nobody catches it; a drop-off-line rant
Playground vs teacher grants vs buses; Yolanda's number is off and gets corrected later
How the vote works; a date gets corrected; a parked question

turns.speaker: Denise
turns.text: Okay, folks, bear with me, my screen share is being difficult. Can everybody see the budget sheet?

turns.speaker: Carl
turns.text: I can see it. It's all in the report, too, if anyone wants the numbers in front of them.

turns.speaker: Denise
turns.text: Great. So, last year first. Carl, the headline?

turns.speaker: Carl
turns.text: Total revenue was forty-eight thousand two hundred, and we spent forty-four nine.

turns.speaker: Brett
turns.text: Here's the thing, I heard we raised sixty grand last year. Where did the rest go?

turns.speaker: Carl
turns.text: With respect, I don't know where you heard—

turns.speaker: Denise
turns.text: Brett, the number's on the sheet. It's forty-eight two.

turns.speaker: Brett
turns.text: Okay, no offense, but people talk. My neighbor was on the board two years ago.

turns.speaker: Carl
turns.text: Two years ago is a different year.

turns.speaker: Yolanda
turns.text: I'm sorry, but can we not start with an accusation? We have a lot to get through.

turns.speaker: Brett
turns.text: I'm not accusing. I'm asking.

turns.speaker: Denise
turns.text: You're both right. Let's look at what's actually left over. Carl?

turns.speaker: Carl
turns.text: The reserve is twelve thousand six hundred. That's after the spring auction cleared.

turns.speaker: Brett
turns.text: Twelve six just sitting in an account while the playground is falling apart.

turns.speaker: Carl
turns.text: A reserve is a reserve. If a fundraiser flops, it covers us.

turns.speaker: Yolanda
turns.text: And the teachers didn't see much of it, for the record.

turns.speaker: Denise
turns.text: How much did the auction actually clear last year?

turns.speaker: Carl
turns.text: Eight four. Lower than the year before.

turns.speaker: Brett
turns.text: Eight four for all that work? Honestly, that's depressing.

turns.speaker: Denise
turns.text: It's a lot of work for that, yes.

turns.speaker: Yolanda
turns.text: Maybe we drop the auction this year.

turns.speaker: Carl
turns.text: Let's not drop anything before we've talked fundraising.

turns.speaker: Denise
turns.text: Okay, folks, fundraising. The fun run is our big one. It brought in about twenty-five thousand last year.

turns.speaker: Carl
turns.text: The fun run is the one I'd never touch.

turns.speaker: Yolanda
turns.text: The kids love it, too. It's the one fundraiser that doesn't feel like begging.

turns.speaker: Brett
turns.text: What about a corporate match thing? My company matches donations.

turns.speaker: Denise
turns.text: Some do. We've never really pushed it.

turns.speaker: Carl
turns.text: It'd be good if somebody made a list of local employers who match.

turns.speaker: Brett
turns.text: I can— actually, never mind, I'm traveling all of October.

turns.speaker: Denise
turns.text: And membership? How many families paid dues this year?

turns.speaker: Carl
turns.text: A hundred and eighty-six. Out of four hundred and twelve kids, so not even half.

turns.speaker: Yolanda
turns.text: Half the families don't know what the PTA does. That's the problem.

turns.speaker: Brett
turns.text: Speaking of things nobody knows, has anyone actually timed the drop-off line? It's twenty-five minutes some mornings.

turns.speaker: Denise
turns.text: Oh, don't get me started on the drop-off line.

turns.speaker: Yolanda
turns.text: The crossing guard is doing her best, I'm sorry, but it's the parents who won't pull forward.

turns.speaker: Brett
turns.text: Here's the thing, it's the minivans. They stop right in the middle to unload backpacks.

turns.speaker: Carl
turns.text: I drive a minivan.

turns.speaker: Denise
turns.text: Okay, folks, the drop-off line is a whole other meeting. Fundraising.

turns.speaker: Yolanda
turns.text: So do we keep the auction or not?

turns.speaker: Carl
turns.text: With respect, the auction is the only fundraiser that grandparents give to.

turns.speaker: Brett
turns.text: Then make it smaller. Fewer baskets, better ones.

turns.speaker: Denise
turns.text: Okay, we keep the fun run, we keep the auction but smaller, and we try the corporate match. That's the plan.

turns.speaker: Yolanda
turns.text: Fine by me.

turns.speaker: Denise
turns.text: I'll call the three biggest local employers about matching before the next meeting.

turns.speaker: Brett
turns.text: If you need a script, I'm happy to write one.

turns.speaker: Denise
turns.text: Okay, the hard part. Spending. Three big asks. Playground, teacher grants, field trips.

turns.speaker: Brett
turns.text: The playground. The resurfacing quote was twenty-two thousand.

turns.speaker: Carl
turns.text: Which is more than our entire reserve.

turns.speaker: Brett
turns.text: Then we raise it. That's literally what a PTA is for.

turns.speaker: Yolanda
turns.text: I'm sorry, but teacher grant requests total twelve thousand, and those are for the kids too.

turns.speaker: Denise
turns.text: Twelve thousand in requests, okay.

turns.speaker: Brett
turns.text: Teachers have a district budget. The playground doesn't.

turns.speaker: Yolanda
turns.text: Do you know what the district budget for my classroom is?

turns.speaker: Brett
turns.text: No, I—

turns.speaker: Yolanda
turns.text: Zero. It's zero. I buy the glue sticks.

turns.speaker: Denise
turns.text: Okay, folks, nobody's saying grants don't matter.

turns.speaker: Carl
turns.text: The classroom grant is two hundred per teacher. That part we always fund.

turns.speaker: Yolanda
turns.text: Two hundred is the floor, not the request.

turns.speaker: Carl
turns.text: Bear with me, I'm looking at the request sheet. The grant requests add up to nine thousand eight hundred, not twelve.

turns.speaker: Yolanda
turns.text: Oh. I had the old list with the smartboard request on it.

turns.speaker: Denise
turns.text: Okay, nine eight. And field trips?

turns.speaker: Yolanda
turns.text: Buses are six fifty each, and we need about twenty trips.

turns.speaker: Brett
turns.text: Can the field trips just be cheaper? Like, closer places?

turns.speaker: Yolanda
turns.text: Closer places are the places they went last year. And the year before.

turns.speaker: Denise
turns.text: What if we fund the grants fully and put the playground in a two-year plan?

turns.speaker: Brett
turns.text: Two years? My kid will be in middle school.

turns.speaker: Carl
turns.text: With respect, that is fiscally the only thing that works.

turns.speaker: Brett
turns.text: Here's the thing, there's a grant for playgrounds. The county does one. Has anyone applied for it?

turns.speaker: Yolanda
turns.text: I'm sorry, but the field trips, we haven't settled the field trips.

turns.speaker: Denise
turns.text: Okay. The teacher grants are funded at nine eight. That part's decided.

turns.speaker: Yolanda
turns.text: Thank you. Honestly, thank you.

turns.speaker: Brett
turns.text: And the playground just waits.

turns.speaker: Denise
turns.text: The playground goes into a two-year plan. Maybe we start with half the resurfacing this year.

turns.speaker: Carl
turns.text: I'll build a two-year version of the budget with the playground split in half, before the vote.

turns.speaker: Brett
turns.text: Fine. But I want it on record that I think it's too slow.

turns.speaker: Yolanda
turns.text: Noted, Brett.

turns.speaker: Denise
turns.text: Last thing. How this gets approved. Carl, remind everyone?

turns.speaker: Carl
turns.text: The board recommends a budget, and then the general membership votes. It's all in the bylaws.

turns.speaker: Brett
turns.text: When's the vote?

turns.speaker: Denise
turns.text: September twentieth.

turns.speaker: Carl
turns.text: Bear with me, it's the twenty-fifth. The twentieth was the original date before the gym conflict.

turns.speaker: Denise
turns.text: The twenty-fifth. Sorry, folks, it's been a week.

turns.speaker: Brett
turns.text: Who decided the reserve has to be that big, anyway?

turns.speaker: Yolanda
turns.text: Can members vote by email, or do they have to be there in person?

turns.speaker: Carl
turns.text: In person or by proxy. It's in the—

turns.speaker: Brett
turns.text: In the bylaws. We know.

turns.speaker: Carl
turns.text: Well, it is.

turns.speaker: Denise
turns.text: Okay. Could someone send the proposed budget to the membership a week before the vote?

turns.speaker: Carl
turns.text: I'll email the proposed budget to every member family by the eighteenth.

turns.speaker: Brett
turns.text: Should we do a playground info table at the vote, so people understand the plan?

turns.speaker: Denise
turns.text: Maybe. Let's see how the two-year version looks first.

turns.speaker: Yolanda
turns.text: Sorry, Denise, my son needs help with his math, one second.

turns.speaker: Denise
turns.text: Go, go, it's fine.

turns.speaker: Yolanda
turns.text: Okay, I'm back. Sorry.

turns.speaker: Denise
turns.text: Okay, folks. I think that's it. Thank you all for coming, even the heated parts.

turns.speaker: Brett
turns.text: Especially the heated parts.

turns.speaker: Carl
turns.text: Goodnight, everyone.
